ACCEPTANCE CRITERION, CHECKED AGAINST THE ACTUAL CANDIDATE

Real owner inspection. tools/publication_decision.py dispatches publication-inspect and publication-decide from tools/job_manager.py:main, which stack_command.py reaches as the installed `manager` verb (COMMANDS["manager"] -> job_manager.main), the same chain as the already-accepted cancel-job / recovery-decide verbs; both new tool modules are reached by static imports PyInstaller's analysis follows, so no spec hiddenimports entry was needed. The focused cases drive these verbs through tools.job_manager.main with operator argv, so parsing, operand checks, store roles and the printed document are the deployment's own. Inspect opens the Job store, control store and Authority read-only; decide opens only the Job store writably.

Exact original output as trust root. The only door is the new worker_manager/workspaces.py:retained_output_of, which before reading a byte proves the deployment's configured workspace storage, positive writer cessation through settlement_preparation (I read that function: it refuses outright with no completed preparation record, and refuses on any unsettled preparation/allocation/removal/cleanup/adoption/maintenance or standing custody overlap), refuses a non-attempt layout rather than guessing, refuses links at home and workspace via custody._no_link, and compares the live device:inode against the identity the completed preparation recorded. The named entries are then read on an O_NOFOLLOW/O_NONBLOCK descriptor with the size checked on the fstat and the content re-digested against the measurement. There is no path, attempt, manifest or digest operand anywhere on the CLI surface -- the selectors are Job, stage, episode and the attempt is resolved from the episode row and cross-bound against the stage's Work -- so an agent copy or a typed path cannot become the trust root. Negative cases I read and that pass: removed original, workspace renamed aside so the replacement cannot inherit the inode (runtime-observation/identity-mismatch, "replaced object"), an admitted-and-unfinished cleanup, uncertain host runtime, a host with no record of the attempt, a frozen result (refused as not this trigger), and a present completion envelope.
